title: Quantization of the classical Mpemba effect
authors: Jannis Melles, Hartmut Löwen, Benno Liebchen, Michael te Vrugt, Giovanna Morigi, Artur Widera, Alexander P. Antonov
abstract: The Mpemba effect refers to the counterintuitive phenomenon that an initially hot system can freeze faster than an initially warm one. Recent years have brought major advances in both classical and quantum realizations, with the asymmetric bistable potential emerging as the paradigmatic classical benchmark because its mechanism is especially transparent and controllable. Yet for precisely this benchmark problem, the impact of quantization remains unexplored. Here we show that quantization shifts Mpemba behavior to qualitatively new regimes, moving it to ultra-cold temperatures that are orders of magnitude lower than those relevant for classical thermal barrier crossing. In addition, quantization produces inverse and double inverse Mpemba effects that are absent in the corresponding classical dynamics. Our results establish quantization as a robust route to quantum-enabled Mpemba effects inaccessible in classical regimes.
summary: The paper theoretically explores the quantization of the Mpemba effect using a bistable potential model. It demonstrates that moving from classical to quantum descriptions fundamentally alters the cooling dynamics, predicting novel effects like inverse and double inverse Mpemba behavior at ultra-low temperatures. This establishes quantization as a robust mechanism for observing anomalous thermal relaxation inaccessible classically.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Mpemba effect—the counterintuitive phenomenon of faster cooling for initially hotter systems—by analyzing its behavior when quantized.
main_result: Quantization shifts the Mpemba effect to ultra-cold temperatures and generates novel quantum phenomena, such as inverse and double inverse Mpemba effects, absent in classical dynamics.
method: The analysis compares classical thermal evolution (using Boltzmann weights) with quantum relaxation governed by Lindblad master equations and spectral decomposition of the Liouvillian operator.
model_or_system: The study uses the paradigmatic benchmark of an asymmetric bistable potential, modeling both classical thermal states and quantum dissipative dynamics.
key_observables: Domain occupation probabilities ($P_L(T)$ or $P_1(T)$), relaxation time ($	au$), and the trace distance quantifying approach to steady state.
important_parameters: Temperature (especially ultra-cold regimes), potential barrier height ($V_0$), and coupling strength determining weak vs. strong coupling limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on single-mode approximations for relaxation dynamics and assumes the existence of weakly coupled states to observe quantum effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-monotonic temperature dependence required for the Mpemba effect in both classical (Fig. 2) and quantum settings, showing different regimes like inverse or double inverse effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the classical benchmark using thermal barrier crossing, then introduces quantization via Lindblad dynamics, deriving the time evolution of population imbalance, and finally comparing the resulting temperature dependencies to highlight novel quantum regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium statistical mechanics in open quantum systems, providing concrete predictions for anomalous relaxation phenomena accessible only through quantum coherence or dissipation mechanisms.
